title: Past Subjunctive
description: Master the imperfect subjunctive (past subjunctive) for unreal or hypothetical situations in the past.

grammar.title: Past Subjunctive Formation
grammar.content:
Past Subjunctive (Imperfect Subjunctive) has two acceptable forms:

-ra form and -se form (both are correct and interchangeable)

FORMATION: Take 3rd person plural of preterite, remove -ron, add endings:

-RA ENDINGS:
hablara, hablaras, hablara, hablramos, hablarais, hablaran
comiera, comieras, comiera, comieramos, comierais, comieran
viviera, vivieras, viviera, vivieramos, vivierais, vivieran

-SE ENDINGS (more formal/literary):
hablase, hablases, hablase, hablacemos, hablaseis, hablasen

Irregulars:
Ser → fuera/fulse
Ir → fuera/fulse (same as ser)
Tener → tuviera/tuviese
Hacer → hiciera/hiciese
Venir → viniera/viniese
Poder → pudiera/pudiese
Querer → quisiera/quisisese
Saber → supiera/supiese
Decir → dijera/dijese

Examples:
Si tuviera dinero, compraria una casa. (If I had money, I would buy a house.)
Quieren que vinieras a la fiesta. (They want you to come to the party.)
examples: Si tuviera tiempo, estudiara mas. (If I had time, I would study more.)
Ojalia el hubiera llegado a tiempo. (I wish he had arrived on time.)
No crei que supieras la respuesta. (I didn't think you knew the answer.)
Esperaba que hicieras la tarea. (I was hoping you would do the homework.)

grammar.title: Uses of Past Subjunctive
grammar.content:
Past subjunctive is used in the SAME situations as present subjunctive, but for PAST or HYPOTHETICAL meanings:

1. AFTER PAST MAIN VERBS expressing will/wish/emotion:
Quise que vinieras. (I wanted you to come.)
Me alegro de que hayas llegado. (I'm glad you have arrived.) — present perfect subjunctive

2. SI CLAUSES for unreal/hypothetical conditions:
Si yo fuera rico, viajaria. (If I were rich, I would travel.)
Si ella supiera, te ayudaria. (If she knew, she would help you.)

3. HYPOTHETICAL STATEMENTS:
Yo que tu, lo hiciera. (I in your place, I would do it.)
Como si fuera verdad. (As if it were true.)

4. AFTER IMPERSONAL EXPRESSIONS in past:
Era importante que estudiaras. (It was important that you study.)

Note: Both -ra and -se forms are acceptable. In everyday speech, -ra is more common in Spain, while -se is considered more formal.
examples: Si yo supiera la respuesta, te la diria. (If I knew the answer, I would tell you.)
Si el hubiera venido, le hubiera dicho la verdad. (If he had come, I would have told him the truth.)
Me gustaria que vinieras a visitarnos. (I would like you to come visit us.)
Era necesario que llegaras temprano. (It was necessary that you arrive early.)

grammar.title: Si Clauses with Past Subjunctive
grammar.content:
SI + Past Subjunctive = unreal/hypothetical condition in present or future

PRESENT UNREAL:
Si yo tuviera dinero, compraria un coche. (If I had money [but I don't], I would buy a car.)

FUTURE UNREAL:
Si yo ganara la loteria, viajaria por el mundo. (If I were to win the lottery, I would travel the world.)

PAST UNREAL (would have):
Si yo hubiera estudiado, habria aprobado. (If I had studied, I would have passed.)

Alternative past unreal with -ra:
Si yo hubiera estudiado, hubiera aprobado. (Both clauses with past perfect subjunctive)

IMPORTANT: After SI expressing HYPOTHESIS, NEVER use conditional or future in the si clause:

INCORRECT: Si yo tendre dinero...
CORRECT: Si yo tuviera dinero...

CONTRAST with real conditions:
REAL: Si estudio, aprobare. (If I study, I will pass.) — possible
UNREAL: Si estudiara, aprobaria. (If I were to study, I would pass.) — hypothetical
examples: Si lloviera mañana, no saldriamos. (If it rained tomorrow, we wouldn't go out.)
Si tuvieras el numero, me llamarias. (If you had the number, you would call me.)
Si hubiera sabido, te hubiera avisado. (If I had known, I would have warned you.)
Si pudiera, te ayudaria con gusto. (If I could, I would help you gladly.)

pronunciation.title: Past Subjunctive Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Past subjunctive endings:

-ra form:
-ara, -aras, -ara, -aramos, -arais, -aran
-iera, -ieras, -iera, -ieramos, -ierais, -ieran

-se form:
-ase, -ases, -ase, -asemos, -aseis, -asen
-iese, -ieses, -iese, -iesemos, -iesesis, -iesen

Key features:
- Stress falls on the syllable BEFORE the ending
- 'iera' and 'iese' both sound like 'yeh-rah'
- 'hubiera' = oo-BYEH-rah
- 'fuera' = FWEH-rah
- 'quisiera' = kee-SYEH-rah

Examples:
hablara = ah-BLAH-rah
comiera = koh-MYEH-rah
viviera = bee-BYEH-rah

Compare with present subjunctive:
hablar → hable (AH-bleh) vs. hablara (ah-BLAH-rah)
comer → coma (KOH-mah) vs. comiera (koh-MYEH-rah)

exercises.question: What is the past subjunctive of 'hablar' for 'yo' (-ra form)?
exercises.explanation: Hablara = I spoke (past subjunctive). Take 'hablaron' (they spoke), remove -ron, add -a.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si yo ___ dinero, compraria un coche. (If I had money, I would buy a car.)'
exercises.explanation: Tuviera = I had (past subjunctive of tener). 'Si yo tuviera' = If I had.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'I wish she had come'?
exercises.explanation: 'Ojalia ella viniera' = I wish she had come (past subjunctive). 'Ojalia' expresses a wish.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Era importante que tu ___ la tarea. (It was important that you do the homework.)'
exercises.explanation: Hicieras = you do (past subjunctive of hacer). After 'era importante que', use subjunctive.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'If I were rich, I would travel'?
exercises.explanation: 'Si fuera rico, viajaria' uses past subjunctive 'fuera' after 'si' for unreal present condition.

exercises.question: Complete: 'No crei que el ___ la respuesta. (I didn't think he knew the answer.)'
exercises.explanation: Supiera = he knew (past subjunctive of saber). After 'no crei que', use subjunctive.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses past subjunctive correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Quise que el viniera' uses past subjunctive 'viniera' after past tense 'quise'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Como si ___ verdad. (As if it were true.)'
exercises.explanation: Fuera = it was (past subjunctive of ser). 'Como si fuera verdad' = As if it were true.

exercises.question: What is the -ra form of past subjunctive for 'ser/ir'?
exercises.explanation: Fuera = I was/went (past subjunctive of ser/ir). Both verbs share the same subjunctive forms.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si ella lo ___ (preterite), me habria enterado. (If she had told me, I would have found out.)'
exercises.explanation: Hubiera dicho = she had said (past perfect subjunctive). This structure expresses unreal past condition.
